04. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners and learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioners are accused in connection with G.R. Case No.01 of 2022 pending on the file of learned Presiding Officer, Designated Court under OPID Act, Berhampur, Ganjam, arising out of EOW Bhubaneswar P.S. Case No.11 of 2022 for commission of offence alleged under Sections 420/406/467/468/471/120-B of IPC read with U/s.66(D) of I.T. Act, Section 4, 5 and 6 of PCMCS (Banning) Act, 1978 and Section 6 of OPID (in Financial Establishments) Act, 2011.

entities.text: EOW Bhubaneswar P.S. Case No.11 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel, on instruction, submits that except the present BLAPL, no other bail applications of the Petitioners relating to the aforementioned P.S. case is pending in any other Court.
4. Being aggrieved by the rejection of their application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Presiding Officer, OPID Court, Berhampur by order dated 20.07.2023 in the aforementioned case,
the present BLAPL has been filed.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioners are in custody since 29.04.2022 and the allegation against them is that assuring higher returns they along with co-accused have duped the investors and there are two accounts which were used for commission of such offence.

The accounts stood in the names of one Kinney InfoTech Pvt. Ltd. in which one Nisha Kashyap W/o Bhiku Bisoyi Chinmaya Kumar Dash And vs State Of Odisha (Opid) .... Opposite ... on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128469753/
1 is the Director and another is Simbucks Virtual Tech Solution (OPC) Pvt. Ltd. which is stated to be a Sister Concern.
6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Simbucks Virtual Tech Solution (OPC) Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is stated in the charge sheet that the following amounts has been transferred from the account of Kinney InfoTech Pvt. Ltd. to the individuals.

Sl Name of the Individuals Amount No 1 Manikandan 1,18,40,000/-
2 Pravat Kumar Dash 7,26,000/-
3 Kinney Info tech Pvt. Ltd. (ICICI) 1,76,50,000/-
 account 4 Simbucks Virtual Tech Solution Pvt. 38,78,500/-
 Ltd. (OPC)

7. It is the further submission of the learned counsel that the Present Petitioners are the employees of that Kinney InfoTech Pvt. Ltd. and because they are the nephew of one director of Kinney InfoTech Pvt. Ltd. namely Bhiku Bisoyi, they have been implicated in the case at hand.

8. Referring to the recitals in paragraph-18.19 of the charge sheet, it is submitted that the present Petitioners are in essence at par with two of the accused persons Rajendra Kumar Gouda and Rajesh Kumar Bhola and since the said accused persons have been released on bail by this Court by order dated 20.12.2022 in BLAPL No.7458 of 2022 (Rajendra Kumar Gouda) and order dated 14.02.2023 in BLAPL No. 6151 of 2022 (Rajesh @ Rajesh Kumar Bhola) Petitioners seek release inter alia on the ground of parity.

9. Learned counsel for the OPID, Mr. Nayak opposes such prayer and submits that the present Petitioners are not similarly placed with the co-accused who have since been released and since the investigation has been kept open U/s.173(8) of the Cr.P.C., release of the present Petitioners considering their proximity to the director, as noted, would derail the ongoing investigation.

10. Taking into account the filing of the charge sheet and the nature of allegation which is primarily based on documentary evidence and the release of the co-accused, as noted, this Court directs the Petitioners to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin.

11. Additionally, taking into account the recitals in the Case Diary, the Petitioner No.2 (Prabhat Kumar Dash @ Pravat) is directed to furnish cash security to the tune of Rs.7,00,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs) as a condition precedent for release.

12. The direction for depositing such amounts is passed taking into account that such amount has been transfered to the account of the Petitioner, as prima facie borne out from the recitals of the Case Diary and the offence in question being an economic offence, in tune with the dictum of the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vrs. Central Bureau of Investigation & another,
reported in 2022 (10) SCC 51.

2 13.

sentences.text: The amount, so deposited, shall be kept in an interest bearing account which shall be abide by the final outcome.
14. Direction for depositing such amount ought not to be construed that this Court expressing any view regarding the complicity of the Petitioners which has to be adjudicated in the impending trail.

15. Since it is submitted, on instruction, that both the Petitioners have no criminal antecedent,
before releasing, the learned Court in seisin is requested to verify the criminal antecedent.
If it comes to the fore that the Petitioners have any criminal antecedent, this order shall not be given effect to.

16. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
17. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
